findings.title: Include identity type in the denial-cache key
findings.body: The denial-cache key uses only the parsed subject ID, omitting IdentityType. Distinct supported subjects such as anonymous:0 and render:0 therefore share a denial entry for the same namespace, action, name, and folder. If an anonymous dashboard read is denied, a subsequent renderer read is also denied for 30 seconds, even though getRendererPermissions grants dashboard reads unconditionally. Include the identity type (or full subject) in this key so one identity cannot poison another identity's authorization checks.

findings.title: Encode denial-cache key components unambiguously
findings.body: Concatenating resource name and parent folder with underscores allows distinct requests to produce the same key. For example, name=a_b with parent=c and name=a with parent=b_c both end in _a_b_c. Underscores are valid in these identifiers, so denying access to one resource can cause an unrelated, permitted resource to be denied until the cache entry expires. Use an unambiguous encoding, such as a serialized tuple or length-prefixed components.
